items.title: AI magic sends markets higher, plus one-on-one with IBM vice chair
items.summary: Today on Sozzi Unleashed, we dive into the market's reaction to Meta's (META) Muse AI, Ray Dalio’s latest warning on a potential AI bubble, and Sozzi’s one-on-one conversation with IBM (IBM) Vice Chair and former US National Economic Council Director Gary Cohn.

items.title: Is Carnival Stock Cheap, Or Is The Cash Already Spoken For?
items.summary: Carnival Corporation (CCL) threw off free cash worth 9.7% of its market value over the last twelve months, more than twice the 4.4% median for an S&P 500 company. A yield that high usually means a bargain or a business the market expects to shrink. Carnival is not that simple. The cash is real, and a large share of it belongs to its lenders.

items.title: Should You Buy Royal Caribbean At A One-Year Low?
items.summary: Royal Caribbean (RCL) trades near $235, at its 52-week low, and over the past year the stock returned about -27% against close to 18% for the S&P 500. The easy read on a cruise line down that far is that demand cracked. It did not. The company lifted its earnings outlook for 2026 and expects adjusted earnings per share to grow 14%, and what has stalled, in the third quarter of 2026, is the price it can put on a cabin.

items.title: Should You Buy Carnival Stock While Europe Sails Emptier?
items.summary: Carnival Corporation (CCL) trades near $22, down about 26% over the past year, while the S&P 500 gained close to 18%. The easy read on a cruise line that cheap is that demand finally cracked. It has not. Carnival lowered its 2026 yield outlook after the Middle East conflict hit its European sailings, and part of that cut was its own choice to protect price rather than fill cabins.

items.title: Iran “Offered” to Reopen the Strait of Hormuz. These Stocks Could Be the Biggest Winners
items.summary: A senior Iranian official told a Japanese news agency that Tehran could reopen one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints within seven days, and the stocks that stand to gain the most are not the ones the market moved on Friday.

items.title: Royal Caribbean Group Falls 5% on $3B Sandals Resorts Stake; Carnival and Norwegian Slide 3%
items.summary: Royal Caribbean just staked billions on a land resort brand, and the market is punishing the stock hard while dragging its cruise rivals down with it. Whether that selloff reflects a smart bet mispriced by panic or a genuine strategic misfire is the question every cruise investor faces this morning.
